# CORE-TGT-05

**Is every building block the target state does not plan for, or holds where it is, brought in or extended only by an exception approved through escalation?**

| | |
|---|---|
| Lens | [Core architecture lens](core.md) 0.6.0 |
| Area | TGT: Target state |
| Default severity | blocker |
| Decided by | A tool, by its rule |
| Reads | `triage.target_state`, `decisions.departure`, `decisions.status` |

## Why it matters

Continuing to use something already in place is a tolerable exception. Bringing in technology that is neither in use nor planned, or giving technology the target state holds where it is a new use, commits the organisation to it, against a target state it has already defined. That is not the responsible architect's decision alone: it is escalated to the exception authority, before the design relies on it, not closed as a gap afterwards.

## Rule

Every element attested at not-target, and every element attested at contained that the design newly relies on (every one, for a new design or a new component; for a change, one the change adds a use of or widens), is named in the affects of a decision with status accepted and departure set, whose departure has escalation recorded and approved_by naming the exception authority the organisation designates (for example the architecture board), not the responsible architect alone. An element at not-target, or a newly relied-on element at contained, with no such decision fails this criterion.

## Sources

- The Open Group, TOGAF Standard 10th Edition, Enterprise Architecture Capability and Governance, chapter 6, Architecture Compliance (`togaf-compliance`)
- The Open Group, G253, Architecture Compliance Review Checklists (2025) (`g253`)
